title: GPU cold-start observations and action sprints — weekly snapshot
content:
Summary:
This week we captured a repeatable cold-start latency pattern across three regions after the standard weekend autoscaler drain. Short version: cold-start P95 spikes correlate with image-layer churn and recent model bundle changes (v2.4.1). We saw region-specific amplification in ap-southeast-1 likely due to slower NFS mounts and an old kernel image on preemptible nodes.

Top-level metrics (observed between 2028-06-10 and 2028-06-16):
- us-west-2: cold-start P50=1.4s, P95=7.2s, mean image pull time ~2.1s
- eu-central-1: cold-start P50=1.7s, P95=9.0s, mean model load time ~3.8s
- ap-southeast-1: cold-start P50=2.6s, P95=18.5s, high variance in disk IO during boot
- baseline warm-request P95 for same models: ~120ms (no change)

Notes from root-cause threads:
- Image churn: two recent PRs increased base image size by ~450MB (runtime deps + new telemetry). Pull time increase tracks linearly with size in regions with slower slices. See PRs in linked_artifacts.
- Model bundle v2.4.1: includes extra tokenizers and small reference datasets; model load time + KV-cache initialize adds ~1.2s on average.
- Node heterogeneity: ap-southeast fleet still has a subgroup with kernel 5.10 which interacts poorly with our preferred NVMe driver; we saw device probe stalls for ~6–12s.
- Preemptible behavior: autoscaler drains at low-util hours — reclaiming prewarmed pools and forcing cold container pulls.

Experiment log (this week's quick runs):
- Pre-warm pool test (small pool): spun up 16 warm workers in us-west-2 for 48h; results: cold-start P95 dropped from 7.2s -> 1.1s for requests hitting warm workers, but cost delta estimated +$0.05/hr per 16 workers.
- Layer-squash image experiment: built a slim image removing unused apt caches; size down 380MB, avg pull time improved ~1.4s in eu-central.
- Model lazy-init: prototype that defers loading optional tokenizers until first call reduced median cold start ~400ms but didn't affect P95 significantly (outliers due to disk stalls).

Operational impact and risk vectoring:
- User-facing SLOs were not violated for warm traffic, but some customers saw request tail latency escalations during region-wide preemptions. Potential impact for streaming chat sessions (partial reconnects).
- Cost vs reliability tradeoff: keeping a minimal warm pool in every region mitigates tail risk but adds persistent cost.

Decisions made in today's sync (informal):
- Short term (2 weeks): create minimal per-region reserve of 8 warm workers (can be autoscaler-exempt) for heavy regions (us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1). Action INFRA-2147.
- Mid term (1–2 months): standardize base image size and move large telemetry libs to optional init step. Action INFRA-2153 + runtime PR 482.
- Long term (Q4): redesign node provisioning to avoid kernel mismatches; target rolling refresh of legacy nodes. Investigate ability to drain without reclaiming all prewarm pools.

Action items (owner, ticket, due):
- Owen Brooks — create autoscaler policy change to exempt warm pool and add health-checks for pool persistence. Ticket: INFRA-2147. Due: 2028-06-24.
- Liang Zhao — finalize layer-squash image and coordinate with registry TTL to avoid double-pulls. PR: runtime#482. Ticket: INFRA-2153. Due: 2028-06-21.
- Priya Menon — run 72h prewarm pilot in ap-southeast-1 and produce cost vs tail-latency graph. Ticket: INFRA-2165. Due: 2028-06-25.
- Samir Kapoor — schedule a node-kernel inventory and put together remediation plan for legacy kernels. Ticket: INFRA-2171. Due: 2028-06-30.

Open questions / discussion items:
- What size warm pool is defensible at scale (per-region)? need to simulate customer traffic profiles (Spike vs steady).
- Can we automatically detect high image-pull latency windows and temporarily shift routing to adjacent regions? (design spike routing policy).
- Is there an opportunity to cache model bundles in a shared network store to avoid full disk load on cold starts? (tradeoffs: network bandwidth vs local NVMe).

Quick wins to try next sprint:
- Add image size gate to PR checklist (CI check that flags >150MB change to base image).
- Back-port NVMe driver config to legacy nodes and roll through a canary set.
- Short-term: raise registry TTL on commonly used model artifacts to reduce redundant pulls during autoscaler churn.

Meeting attendees (today's sync):
- Maya Patel (notes), Owen Brooks, Liang Zhao, Priya Menon, Samir Kapoor, Jenna Ortiz (SRE), Ricardo Alves (solutions-eng - ops impact call-in)

Misc scratch notes (to self):
- Slack thread #infra-gpu-coldstart has some deeper I/O traces; check around 2028-06-12 03:14 UTC (attached).
- Confluence runbook needs new section: "cold start mitigation matrix".
- Low-priority: explore containerd snapshotters that reduce layer extraction time (link in linked_artifacts).

Next sync: 2028-06-21 09:30 PT — 30m follow-up, focus on cost modelling + pilot results.
